title: etbb-july-2024-february-2026-update.pdf — section 245
text:
3. This chapter deals specifically with mental capacity. Where an individual has a mental
disability, but does not lack capacity, see chapter 4.
Criteria for assessing capacity (to conduct litigation)

4. The legal system relies on the assumption that people are capable of making, and therefore
being responsible for, their own decisions and actions. It is therefore necessary to be able to
recognise a lack of mental capacity (or “incapacity”) when it exists, and to cope with the legal
implications.

5. Appearances can be deceptive:
• It is not unusual for communication difficulties to create a false impression of lack of
mental capacity.
• A person’s appearance, perhaps the consequence of physical disabilities, can create an
impression of lack of mental capacity which is not justified.
• Observance of the conventions of society or adopting others’ communication skills, can
disguise lack of capacity (eg a learned behaviour pattern).
